Moksha: Spiritual liberation in Hinduism, Buddhism, Jainism and Sikhism. In its epistemological and psychological senses, moksha requires self-realization, self-actualization, and self-knowledge.
She became the first woman ever elected Speaker of the U.S. House — and the first to lead a major party in either chamber of Congress. Who is she?
This Russian communist politician twice ran unsuccessfully for president against Vladimir Putin, in 2004 and again in 2024 — who is he?
In the Book of Genesis, this son of Judah was struck down for refusing to father a child with his deceased brother's widow, Tamar — who was he?
Onan: Biblical figure; second son of Judah.
He left school at 14 yet became Australia's 24th prime minister, having first served as treasurer under Bob Hawke before taking the top job in 1991 — who is he?
Paul Keating: Prime Minister of Australia from 1991 to 1996.
Educated in New Zealand and the United States, this Thai businessman led the Move Forward Party, successor to the dissolved Future Forward Party — who is he?
Pita Limjaroenrat: Thai businessman and politician (born 1980)
Having conquered all the warring states to unify China by 221 BC, this ruler coined the brand-new title "huangdi" rather than reuse the old word for king — who was he?
Qin Shi Huang: Emperor of China from 221 to 210 BC.

According to the Hebrew Bible, this son of Solomon and grandson of David lost the ten northern tribes to a rebellion around 932 BCE, becoming the first king of the southern Kingdom of Judah — who is he?
Rehoboam: Biblical figure; first monarch of the Kingdom of Judah.
A human-rights lawyer who rode a wave of younger internet users into office, this man served as South Korea's ninth president from 2003 to 2008 — who is he?
Roh Moo-hyun: President of South Korea from 2003 to 2008. Roh's pre-presidential political career was focused on human rights advocacy for student activists in South Korea.
Saleh al-Arouri: Hamas deputy leader (1966–2024). Al-Arouri was born in 'Arura near Ramallah in the West Bank in 1966.

For 17 years Carthage and Rome struggled for Mediterranean supremacy across Italy, Iberia, and North Africa, with Hannibal repeatedly crushing Roman legions before Carthage's eventual defeat — which of their three wars was this?
Second Punic War: War between Rome and Carthage (218–201 BC)
Founded in 1966 by Bal Thackeray as a Marathi nationalist, Hindutva-based movement, this Indian political party split into two rival factions in 2022 — what is it called?
Shiv Sena: Political party in Maharashtra, India.

Lasting from December 1979 to February 1989, this conflict saw mujahideen fighters — backed by Pakistan, the U.S. via Operation Cyclone, and others — battle a Communist superpower and its allied government. What war is it?
Soviet–Afghan War: 1979–1989 armed conflict in South Asia.

First emerging among Spanish and North American workers in the 1870s, this labor movement organizes workers by industry and uses strikes and direct action aiming to seize control of the means of production — what's it called?
A sickly, asthmatic child who built himself up through what he called 'the strenuous life,' he took office after McKinley's assassination as the youngest-ever president — who was he?
Theodore Roosevelt: President of the United States from 1901 to 1909.
Born a peasant, this man rose to become the most powerful figure in Japan and the first person ever to hold the rank of Kampaku without being born a noble — who was this second 'Great Unifier'?
Toyotomi Hideyoshi: Military ruler of Japan from 1585 to 1598.
This philosophy and practice rejects treating animals as commodities, leading its followers to abstain from all animal-derived food, clothing, and entertainment. What is it?

Once a close ally of Sun Yat-sen and celebrated for his part in the 1911 Revolution, this Chinese politician later led a Japanese-backed puppet government in WWII and is remembered by many as a traitor — who is he?
Kenya's current president since 2022, he previously became the country's first elected deputy president after representing Eldoret North in parliament — who is he?

William Ruto: President of Kenya since 2022. William Kipchirchir Samoei Arap Ruto (born 21 December 1966) is a Kenyan politician who is the fifth and current president of Kenya since 13 September 2022.
Before serving two terms as Israel's seventh prime minister, this Polish-born politician had been a leader of the pre-state Zionist militant group Lehi, the so-called Stern Gang — who was he?
Yitzhak Shamir: Prime Minister of Israel (1983–1984; 1986–1992)

This Sanskrit term translating as 'emptiness' or 'voidness' anchors a key Mahāyāna Buddhist tenet, and in Theravāda often points to the non-self nature of the five aggregates of experience — what is it?
Śūnyatā: Philosophical concept of emptiness found in Asian religions.
Who among these was born first?
Patrick Geddes (born 1854) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these people was born first?
Levi Strauss (born 1829) is the earliest of the four.
Which one below was born first?
Maria Goeppert Mayer (born 1906) is the earliest of the four. In 1986, the Maria Goeppert Mayer Award for early-career women physicists was established in her honor.
C (programming language) (founded 1972) is the earliest of the four.
Which one below is best known as an astronomer?
Tycho Brahe is an astronomer. In 1572, Tycho noticed a completely new star that was brighter than any star or planet.
Which of these four is a mathematician?
Robert Aumann is a mathematician. Aumann received the Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences in 2005 for his work on conflict and cooperation through game theory analysis.
What is the atomic number of Molybdenum?
Molybdenum is a chemical element; it has symbol Mo and atomic number 42.
What is the atomic number of Iron?
Iron is a chemical element; it has symbol Fe (from Latin ferrum 'iron') and atomic number 26.
In what year was Neil Armstrong born?
Neil Armstrong: Armstrong was born and raised near Wapakoneta, Ohio.
In what year was Lewis Carroll born?
Lewis Carroll: An avid puzzler, Carroll created the word ladder puzzle, which he called "Doublets", which was published in Vanity Fair magazine between 1879 and 1881.
In what year was Mileva Marić born?
Mileva Marić: Marić and Einstein were study colleagues and lovers, and had a daughter Lieserl in 1902, who likely died of scarlet fever at one and a half years old.
In what year did Jane Goodall die?
Jane Goodall: Dame Valerie Jane Morris Goodall ( GUUD-awl; née Morris-Goodall; 3 April 1934 – 1 October 2025) was an English primatologist and anthropologist.
In what year did Carl Friedrich Gauss die?
Carl Friedrich Gauss: Gauss was director of the Göttingen Observatory in Germany and professor of astronomy from 1807 until his death in 1855.
In what year was Klinefelter syndrome discovered?
Klinefelter syndrome (KS), also known as 47,XXY, is a chromosome anomaly.
Bash (Unix shell): Brian Fox. Bash (short for "Bourne Again SHell") is an interactive command interpreter and command language developed for Unix-like operating systems.
Airbus A220: Bombardier Aerospace. The Airbus A220 is a family of five-abreast narrow-body airliners by Airbus Canada Limited Partnership (ACLP).
In which country is Mitsubishi A6M Zero?
Mitsubishi A6M Zero: Japan. It was operated by the Imperial Japanese Navy (IJN) from 1940 to 1945.
Who is credited with discovering Malaria?
Malaria: Ronald Ross. Malaria is a mosquito-borne infectious disease that is transmitted by the bite of Anopheles mosquitoes.
Who is credited with discovering Kwashiorkor?
Kwashiorkor: Cicely Williams. Kwashiorkor ( KWOSH-ee-OR-kor, -⁠kər) is a form of severe protein malnutrition characterized by edema and an enlarged liver with fatty infiltrates.
Who is credited with discovering Titanium?
Titanium: William Gregor. Titanium is a chemical element; it has symbol Ti and atomic number 22.
Despite the conspiracy buzz, this violet compound is mass-produced, sold to the public, and not a controlled substance — its hemostatic derivative is carbazochrome. What is it?
Adrenochrome is a chemical compound produced by the oxidation of adrenaline (epinephrine).
This white crystalline chemical compound is mainly used as a high-nitrogen agricultural fertilizer, but is also a key ingredient in explosive mixtures used for mining and quarrying — what is it?
Ammonium nitrate is a chemical compound with the formula NH4NO3.
Linked to smoking, high blood pressure and older age, this silent widening of the body's main artery to over 1.5 times normal size can suddenly rupture with severe abdominal pain — what condition?
Aortic aneurysm is an enlargement (dilatation) of the aorta to greater than 1.5 times normal size.
This American psychologist developed the philosophy of radical behaviorism and pioneered operant conditioning while a longtime professor at Harvard — who is he?
B. F. Skinner (March 20, 1904 - August 18, 1990) was an American psychologist, behaviorist, inventor, and social philosopher.

The bassist of a legendary British rock band from 1962 to 1993, performing on its first 19 studio albums, this musician was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 1989 as part of that group — who is he?
Bill Wyman (n Perks; born 24 October 1936) is an English musician who was the bassist of the rock band the Rolling Stones from 1962 to 1993.

Named for its bread-like texture and potato-like flavor when cooked, this tropical tree fruit spread through Oceania via ancient seafaring migrations before European navigators brought Polynesian varieties to the Caribbean — which fruit?
Breadfruit (Artocarpus altilis) is a species of flowering tree in the mulberry and jackfruit family (Moraceae).
Wolves, domestic dogs, coyotes, and golden jackals all belong to this taxonomic genus, whose members are known for massive skulls, long legs, and short ears and tails. Name the genus?
Canis is a genus of the Caninae which includes multiple extant species, such as wolves, dogs, coyotes, and golden jackals.
Which American political scientist drew fierce controversy as co-author of the 1994 book 'The Bell Curve' and author of the welfare-system critique 'Losing Ground'?
Charles Murray (political scientist) (born January 8, 1943) is an American political scientist.
Almost instantly after a vessel is injured, platelets swarm and fibrin cross-links to turn blood from liquid to gel, stopping the leak so repair can begin. What's the name for this clotting process?
Coagulation is the process by which blood changes from a liquid to a gel forming a blood clot.
Going by puma, mountain lion, catamount, and panther depending on the region, this big cat is the most widely distributed wild land mammal in the Western Hemisphere — what is it?
Cougar (Puma concolor), also called puma, mountain lion, catamount, and panther, is a large feline native to the Americas.
Marked by a telltale skin rash plus progressive muscle weakness, this systemic autoimmune condition can also bring fever, weight loss and light sensitivity — which disease?
Dermatomyositis (DM) is a group of sytemic autoimmune inflammatory diseases primarily affecting the skin and skeletal muscles.
Partly blinded in a childhood fishing accident, this Alabama-born naturalist turned to insects, co-developed the theory of island biogeography, and founded the field of sociobiology. Who is he?
E. O. Wilson (June 10, 1929 - December 26, 2021) was an American biologist, naturalist, ecologist, and entomologist who developed the field of sociobiology.

This is the only living group of horses, asses, and zebras — odd-toed, herbivorous mammals whose ancestors first evolved in North America before spreading into Asia, Africa, and South America — what is it?
Equus (genus) is a genus of mammals in the perissodactyl family Equidae, which includes horses, asses, and zebras.
Also badged as the Citroën Jumper and the Peugeot Boxer in Europe, this light commercial van entered North America in 2014 as the Ram ProMaster — which van?
Fiat Ducato is a light commercial vehicle jointly developed by FCA Italy and PSA Group (now Stellantis), and mainly manufactured by Sevel, a joint venture between the two companies since 1981.

A bulbous Allium native to Central Asia and northeastern Iran, this kitchen staple counts the chive, leek, and shallot among its cousins and was prized by ancient Babylonians and Egyptians — what is it?
Garlic (Allium sativum) is a species of bulbous flowering plants in the genus Allium.
This large, semi-bitter citrus fruit originated in Barbados as an accidental 18th-century hybrid of the sweet orange and the pomelo, and has also been called the 'forbidden fruit.' What is it?
Grapefruit (Citrus paradisi) is a subtropical citrus tree known for its relatively large, sour to semi-sweet, somewhat bitter fruit.

Known as 'The Last Universalist' for mastering nearly every branch of his field, this French mathematician and physicist founded modern chaos theory through his study of the three-body problem — who is he?
Henri Poincaré (29 April 1854 - 17 July 1912) was a French mathematician, theoretical physicist, engineer, and philosopher of science.
Often confused with a benign tumor, this cell-proliferation process increases an organ's cell count rather than the size of each cell — which term?

Hyperplasia (from Ancient Greek (hupr) 'over' and (plsis) 'formation'), or hypergenesis, is an enlargement of an organ or tissue caused by an increase in the amount of tissue that results from cell proliferation.
With the formula Fe2O3, this reddish inorganic compound occurs naturally as the mineral hematite, a key raw material for the steel industry — which compound?
Iron(III) oxide is the inorganic compound with the formula Fe2O3. It occurs in nature as the mineral hematite, which serves as the primary source of iron for the steel industry.
This Johns Hopkins psychologist coined the terms 'gender role' and 'sexual orientation' and believed gender was malleable during a child's first two years. Who was he?
John Money (8 July 1921 - 7 July 2006) was a New Zealand American psychologist, sexologist and professor at Johns Hopkins University known for his research on human sexual behavior and gender.
Striking children as they wean, up to about age five, this protein-deficiency disorder produces edema and a fatty, enlarged liver — what is it called?
Kwashiorkor (-kr) is a form of severe protein malnutrition characterized by edema and an enlarged liver with fatty infiltrates.
Sociable for a big cat and more active by day than its relatives, this savannah hunter is so sexually dimorphic that only the males grow a sweeping mane. Which animal?
Lion (Panthera leo) is a large cat of the genus Panthera, currently ranging only in Sub-Saharan Africa and India.

This German sexologist founded the Scientific-Humanitarian Committee, which carried out what's been called the first advocacy for homosexual and transgender rights — before the Nazis stripped his citizenship in 1933. Who was he?
Magnus Hirschfeld (14 May 1868 - 14 May 1935) was a German physician, sexologist, and LGBTQ advocate whose German citizenship was revoked in 1933 by the Nazi government.
Shaped like a half-moon, this crescent of fibrocartilage partly divides the knee joint and also turns up in the wrist, jaw, and shoulder joints — what is it called?
Meniscus (anatomy) (pl.: menisci or meniscuses) is a crescent-shaped fibrocartilaginous anatomical structure that, in contrast to an articular disc, only partly divides a joint cavity.
With over 86,000 living species spanning sea, freshwater, and even land, this is the largest of all marine phyla — what is it?
Mollusca is a phylum of protostomic invertebrate animals, whose members are known as molluscs or mollusks.

The first recognized fossil of this archaic human group was unearthed in 1856 in a German valley, and the species vanished around 40,000 years ago as modern humans arrived; who were these Pleistocene Europeans?

Neanderthal (nee-(r)-TAHL, nay-, -THAHL; Homo neanderthalensis or sometimes Homo sapiens neanderthalensis) are an extinct group of archaic humans who inhabited Europe and Western and Central Asia during the Middle to Late Pleistocene.
First described by Linnaeus in 1758, this medium-sized spotted cat of the Americas is a skilled climber, leaper, and swimmer that hunts armadillos and opossums by night — which cat is it?
Ocelot (Leopardus pardalis) is a medium-sized spotted wild cat that reaches 40-50 cm (16-20 in) at the shoulders and weighs between 7 and 15.5 kg (15 and 34 lb) on average.
Located above, below, between, and behind the eyes, these four paired air-filled cavities take their names from the skull bones that contain them — what are they?
Paranasal sinuses are a group of four paired air-filled spaces that surround the nasal cavity.
This inflammation of the back of the throat causes a sore throat and fever, most often from a viral infection, though strep bacteria cause roughly a quarter of cases in children — name the condition?
Pharyngitis is inflammation of the back of the throat, known as the pharynx.
This radioactive, silvery-gray actinide metal with atomic number 94 forms oxides in moist air that can expand a sample by up to 70% in volume — which element?
Plutonium is a chemical element; it has symbol Pu and atomic number 94.
Discovered in 1915 and too faint to see with the naked eye, which small, dim star, orbiting its two brighter neighbors once every 550,000 years, is our closest stellar neighbor after the Sun?
Proxima Centauri is the nearest star to Earth after the Sun, located 4.25 light-years (1.3 parsecs) away in the southern constellation of Centaurus.
Belonging to the genus Ribes and native to western Europe, which berry carries the scientific name Ribes rubrum and has spread into the wild in many regions?
Redcurrant (Ribes rubrum) is a member of the genus Ribes in the family Grossulariaceae.
Sitting in group 4 just below hafnium, this synthetic element named for a famous physicist has a most-stable isotope that survives only about 48 minutes — which element is it?
Rutherfordium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Rf and atomic number 104.
Coined by Horace Walpole in 1754, this term describes an unplanned fortunate discovery, as with penicillin or the microwave oven — what is it called?
Serendipity is an unplanned fortunate discovery. The concept is often associated with scientific and technological breakthroughs, where accidental discoveries led to new insights or inventions.
This Polish-American Gestalt psychologist insisted 'most social acts lose meaning if isolated' — a credo that shaped his famous experiments on conformity and impression formation. Who was he?
Solomon Asch (September 14, 1907 - February 20, 1996) was a Polish-American Gestalt psychologist and pioneer in social psychology.
This artificial sweetener is produced by chlorinating ordinary table sugar and is roughly 600 times sweeter than sucrose — three times sweeter even than aspartame — what's the sweetener called?

Sucralose is an artificial sweetener and sugar substitute. The commercial success of sucralose-based products stems from its favorable comparison to other low-calorie sweeteners in terms of taste, stability, and safety.
A colorless, water-miscible cyclic ether and a versatile solvent, this compound is mainly used as a precursor to polymers and is an isomer of butanone — what is it?
Tetrahydrofuran (THF), or oxolane, is an organic compound with the formula (CH2)4O.
When water loss to the air outpaces uptake by the roots, plants shut tiny leaf pores to conserve moisture, slowing this evaporative water-movement process — what's it called?
Transpiration is the process of water movement through a plant and its evaporation from aerial parts, such as leaves, stems and flowers.

Named after an 18th-century Italian physicist and first published in 1797, this phenomenon explains why fluid pressure drops as it speeds up through a narrower pipe section — powering wine aerators and vacuum ejectors. What is it called?
Venturi effect is the reduction in fluid pressure that results when a moving fluid speeds up as it is funneled from one section of a pipe to another, smaller section.
Chairman of the Polish People's Party since 2015 and a former Minister of Labour and Social Affairs, this physician-turned-politician ran for the Polish presidency in 2020 — who is he?
Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz (born 10 August 1981) is a Polish physician and politician, who has served as the Deputy Prime Minister of Poland, and Minister of National Defence since 2023.
The simplest alkyne, this colorless gas packs all four of its atoms into one straight line thanks to a carbon-carbon triple bond, and fuels welding torches — which compound is it?
First nominated by Ronald Reagan in 1987 and reappointed every four years until 2006, this soft-spoken economist logged the second-longest tenure ever as chairman of the Federal Reserve — who was he?
Alan Greenspan: American economist and financial advisor (born 1926)
Nicknamed the boto for its rosy pink hue (especially in males), this South American toothed whale is the largest species of its kind found in a freshwater habitat — what is it?
Amazon river dolphin: Species of toothed whale. The position of the Araguaian river dolphin (I. araguaiaensis) within the clade is still unclear.
This American anthropologist studied women's weaving and blacksmithing work in Indonesia and later designed microcredit programs to fight rural poverty — who was she?
Native to the Philippines and spread by Austronesian voyagers as early as 1500 BCE, this palm's fruit is chewed with slaked lime and betel leaves for its stimulant effects — which species?
Areca catechu: Species of palm. It was carried widely through the tropics by the Austronesian migrations and trade since at least 1500 BCE due to its use in betel nut chewing.
Developed to herd livestock across rough terrain by nipping at their heels, this short-coated working breed's coat reads as either 'red' or 'blue' — which breed?

Australian Cattle Dog: Breed of herding dog. The Australian Cattle Dog, or simply Cattle Dog, is a breed of herding dog developed in Australia for droving cattle over long distances across rough terrain.

This relationship, expressed as A = εcl, links how much light a solution absorbs directly to its concentration — what is this principle called, named after two scientists whose work dates back to the mid-18th century?
Beer–Lambert law: Scientific law describing absorption of light.
Long-tailed and originally from the Indian subcontinent, this whiskered rodent is a major agricultural pest yet is honored as sacred at the Karni Mata Temple in India — which species is it?
Black rat: Species of rodent. It is a generalist omnivore that can live on a wide variety of foods.
Distinguished by a cube-shaped body, this class of stinging cnidarians includes species such as Chironex fleckeri, whose venom is often fatal to humans — what is it?
Box jellyfish: Class of cnidarians distinguished by their cube-shaped medusae.
Designed in 1959 and partly based on Grace Hopper's FLOW-MATIC, this English-like programming language still runs mainframe banking systems today — what is it?
COBOL: Programming language with English-like syntax.
This involuntary, striated tissue forms the thick middle layer of the heart wall, with individual cells joined by structures called intercalated discs — what is it?
Cardiac muscle: Muscular tissue of heart in vertebrates.

Making up the brain's outer layer of neural tissue, this six-layered structure handles attention, memory, language, and consciousness, and is folded to fit more surface area inside the skull — what is it called?
Cerebral cortex: Outer layer of the cerebrum of the mammalian brain.

An essential nutrient your liver can only partly produce on its own, this compound builds phospholipids in cell membranes and helps make a neurotransmitter for muscle control, and occurs naturally in eggs, meat, and fish — which nutrient?
Choline: Chemical compound and essential nutrient. Choline is a cation with the chemical formula [(CH3)3NCH2CH2OH]+.
The smallest member of the cockatoo family and native to Australia, this crested pet bird is kept in an estimated 4.8 million US households — what bird is it?
Cockatiel: Species of bird. It is, therefore, now classified as the smallest subfamily of the Cacatuidae (cockatoo family).
Nicknamed the shaggy mane or lawyer's wig, this scaly white mushroom dissolves itself into black ink just hours after being picked — which fungus?
Coprinus comatus: Species of fungus. The young fruit bodies first appear as white cylinders emerging from the ground, then the bell-shaped caps open out.
Sold under trade names like Super Glue and Krazy Glue, this fast-acting adhesive family rapidly polymerizes the moment it contacts water — which chemical group?
Cyanoacrylate: Type of fast-acting adhesive. The cyanoacrylate group in the monomer rapidly polymerizes in the presence of water to form long, strong chains.
With evidence of practice dating back to 7000 BC, this field is considered the very first specialization to branch off from general medicine — what is it?
Dentistry: Branch of medicine. Dentistry, also known as dental medicine and oral medicine, is the branch of medicine focused on the teeth, gums, and mouth.
Nicknamed 'Spad' after a World War I fighter, this piston-engine attack plane flew from 1946 into the 1980s, an anachronism deep into the Jet Age — which aircraft?
Douglas A-1 Skyraider: American single engine attack aircraft.
Linked with orgasm and involving involuntary pelvic-floor contractions, this male bodily process can even happen during sleep as a so-called 'wet dream' — what is it?
Ejaculation: Semen discharge from the male reproductive tract.
This 1939 Nobel Physics laureate invented the cyclotron and went on to found two national laboratories that carry his surname today — who was he?

Scientifically known as Chloris chloris, this small finch is widespread across Europe, North Africa, and Southwest Asia, and has also been introduced to Australia, New Zealand, Uruguay, and Argentina — what bird is this?
European greenfinch: Species of bird. The European greenfinch or simply the greenfinch (Chloris chloris) is a small passerine bird in the finch family Fringillidae.
Also called slapped cheek syndrome, this common childhood illness is caused by parvovirus B19, discovered in 1975 — what condition is it?
Fifth disease: Red rash due to infection with parvovirus B19.
Known online by the alias TiAMO, this Swede co-founded a notorious file-sharing site and stood trial for it in 2009, a saga captured in the documentary TPB AFK — who is he?
This field studies how geography shapes international relations and foreign policy, though critics have dismissed its early theories as pseudoscience — which discipline?
Geopolitics: Study of geography's effects on politics.
This plant genus in the mallow family gives us cotton, humanity's primary natural fiber, with its name tracing to an Arabic word for a soft substance — which genus?
Gossypium: Genus of flowering plants in the mallow family Malvaceae.

Derived independently in the 1830s by two European researchers and later given theoretical backing by George Stokes, this law describes the pressure drop of laminar flow through a drinking straw or a hypodermic needle — what's it called?
Hagen–Poiseuille equation: Law describing the pressure drop in an incompressible and Newtonian fluid.

Governed by rules laid out in a document called a blazon, this medieval discipline of coats of arms, crests, and mottoes may have arisen so knights could recognize commanders behind their helmets — what is it?
Heraldry: Discipline of the design and study of coats of arms.
Running from your shoulder to your elbow, this long arm bone has a constriction nicknamed the 'surgical neck' due to its tendency to fracture — which bone?
Humerus: Long bone of the upper arm. It connects the scapula and the two bones of the lower arm, the radius and ulna, and consists of three sections.

Trained originally as a naval architect before becoming a self-taught nuclear physicist, this scientist directed the Soviet Union's atomic bomb program and earned the nickname 'father of the Russian bomb' — who is he?
This tech entrepreneur co-founded Twitter, later built a fintech company behind Square, Cash App, and Tidal, and also helped launch the decentralized network Bluesky?
This English scientist's 1808 book, 'A New System of Chemical Philosophy,' laid the foundations of modern atomic theory, and he also kept daily weather records for over fifty years — who was he?
John Dalton: British chemist and physicist (1766–1844)
Patented in 1967 and approved for medical use in 1980, this propionic-acid-class NSAID works by blocking prostaglandin production — what is it?
Known by common names like true lavender and English lavender despite not being native to England, this Mediterranean-basin plant belongs to the mint family — which species?
Lavandula angustifolia: Species of plant. Lavandula angustifolia, formerly L. officinalis, is a flowering plant in the family Lamiaceae, native to the Mediterranean basin.
Also known as the deer ked, this blood-sucking fly sheds its own wings once it lands on a host and burrows through the fur to feed — what species is it?
Lipoptena cervi: Species of fly. Lipoptena cervi, the deer ked or deer fly, is a species of biting fly in the family of louse flies, Hippoboscidae.
This common, nonspecific medical sign involves lymph nodes becoming abnormally swollen or enlarged, with causes ranging from the common cold to cancer. What's the condition called?
Lymphadenopathy: Abnormal change in size of the lymph nodes.
A student of Marie Curie, this French physicist discovered the element francium in 1939 and later became the first woman elected to the French Académie des Sciences — who was she?
Typically running 21 to 35 days, this coordinated dance of estrogen and progesterone prepares the uterine lining and releases an egg to make pregnancy possible — what is it?
Menstrual cycle: Natural changes in the human female reproductive system.
Known to NATO as 'Flogger,' this Soviet variable-sweep-wing fighter was the first in the country's air force to carry look-down/shoot-down radar, with over 5,000 built. Which aircraft?
Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-23: Soviet fighter-interceptor aircraft introduced in 1970.
Born in China and educated at MIT and Stanford, this billionaire engineer founded Taiwan's dominant chipmaker, serving as its CEO from 1987 to 2005 — who is he?
Morris Chang: Taiwanese businessman and electrical engineer (born 1931)

The males of this stocky Arctic cetacean sport a spiralled 'tusk' up to three metres long — actually a protruding left canine tooth thought to work as a weapon, a tool, and maybe a salinity sensor. What animal is it?
A child prodigy turned MIT mathematician, this American is regarded as the originator of cybernetics — the science of communication in living things and machines — who was he?
Norbert Wiener: American mathematician and philosopher (1894–1964)

Found above 3,500 metres on the Tibetan Plateau, this parasitic fungus grows out of moth larvae and is prized — despite containing arsenic — as an aphrodisiac in traditional Chinese medicine. What is it commonly called?
Ophiocordyceps sinensis: Species of fungus. It parasitizes larvae of ghost moths and produces a fruiting body which is valued in traditional Chinese medicine and Nepalese medicine as an aphrodisiac.
From a single western-Mediterranean flowering plant come both a notorious drug and the tiny dark seeds sprinkled on your bagel — which species is it?
Papaver somniferum: Species of flowering plant in the poppy family.

This term for 'parts in each thousand' is symbolized by ‰ — a percent sign with an extra zero — and sits right next to the percent sign in Unicode's General Punctuation block — what is this unit called?
Per mille: Unit for parts per thousand. The associated symbol is ‰, similar to a per cent sign % but with an extra zero in the divisor.

Also known as physiography, this branch of natural science studies the atmosphere, hydrosphere, biosphere, and geosphere — as opposed to the branch focused on the built human environment. Which field of study?
Physical geography: Study of processes and patterns in the natural environment.
This large, structurally diverse family of plant compounds includes flavonoids and tannic acid, some of which were historically used as dyes and for tanning garments — what are they called?
Also called cherry laurel, this evergreen shrub native to the Black Sea region was once woven into wreaths for its resemblance to true bay laurel, though the two aren't closely related — which plant?
Prunus laurocerasus: Species of plant. It is not to be confused with its American relative Prunus caroliniana, which is also called cherry laurel.
The largest of the procyonid family, this North American mammal is famous for its facial mask, ringed tail, and remarkably dexterous front paws — which animal is it?
Raccoon: Medium-sized mammal native to North America.
Discovered in 1803 by William Hyde Wollaston and named for the rose color of one of its compounds, this rare silvery-white metal of the platinum group is used to enhance jewelry — which element?
